theme: Airbnb API wrappers and search-page clients (catalogue only, never run): pyairbnb, airbnb-scraper, airbnb search results parsers; note what fields they expose

candidates.name: pyairbnb
candidates.what_it_holds: Python package (149 stars, 46 forks, 102 commits, MIT, updated ~22 days ago as of scout date) that hits Airbnb's own public GraphQL/JSON endpoints (no auth/login needed) to pull: search results (filterable by price, amenities, cancellation policy, room type), per-night price for given check-in/out, month-by-month calendar availability, reviews (text+rating), host detail, and Experiences listings. No committed dataset; live pull only.
candidates.why_useful: Most actively maintained, highest-star pure-Python Airbnb client found. If a human decides scraping Airbnb search/calendar pages is in scope, this is the reference implementation for pulling nightly price and calendar-availability fields at scale (relevant to gap #2, realised ADR/occupancy) and for search-result counts as a nights/supply proxy. Method only, not data.
candidates.geography: global (67 country domains per its own docs lineage)

candidates.name: pybnb (johnbalvin)
candidates.what_it_holds: Earlier/sibling Python Airbnb scraper by the same author as pyairbnb (52 stars, updated Nov 2024). Likely an earlier iteration with overlapping field coverage (search, listing, calendar, price).
candidates.why_useful: Secondary/older version of pyairbnb; catalogue for completeness in case pyairbnb regresses a field this one still has.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: superseded by pyairbnb from the same author

candidates.name: gobnb
candidates.what_it_holds: Go-language port of the same author's Airbnb scraper (39 stars, 22 commits, MIT, updated Jul 2025). Extracts room-level listing data (price, check-in/out, images), and search results by geographic coordinates/zoom level, optimized for airbnb.com/rooms/[roomID] URLs.
candidates.why_useful: Same field coverage as pyairbnb but in Go for higher-throughput pulls if a human authorizes scraping; useful if Python client breaks against a schema change since it's independently maintained.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: same author/field-set as pyairbnb, different language

candidates.name: airbnb-python (nderkach)
candidates.what_it_holds: 203-star, 67-fork unofficial Python wrapper around Airbnb's old official partner/mobile API (WTFPL licence, 43 commits). Endpoints: user profile (auth required), listing availability calendar, listing reviews, home search by city or GPS coordinates.
candidates.why_useful: Long-standing, widely-forked reference for calendar+review+search fields; useful as a fallback/second implementation to cross-check pyairbnb's field names, though the underlying API it targets is likely partly deprecated (Airbnb closed most of its public partner API years ago) so it may need patching before any human decides to run it.
candidates.time_coverage: live/point-of-scrape only; API surface likely stale

candidates.name: airbnbapi (zxol)
candidates.what_it_holds: 227-star, 53-fork Node.js wrapper around Airbnb's private mobile-app API (MIT, 107 commits). Exposes: property search with filters, public+private listing detail, host summaries/active listings, public calendar/pricing AND private calendar management (reservations, blocked days, dynamic pricing per date), guest/host user info, messaging threads, review submission, and batch reservation retrieval (host-side, needs auth token).
candidates.why_useful: Highest-star Airbnb API client found in this sweep; documents the richest field set (including host-side reservation/calendar internals) of any repo surveyed, useful as a reference for what fields Airbnb's own app exposes even if never run — e.g. confirms per-date dynamic pricing and blocked-day calendar fields exist server-side, which bears on how realised ADR/occupancy could in principle be reconstructed (gap #2).

candidates.name: airbnb-scraper (digital-engineering)
candidates.what_it_holds: 210-star Scrapy-based 'Advanced Airbnb Search' scraper (Python, GPL-3.0, updated Oct 2022, now explicitly unmaintained per its own README). Extracts property names/descriptions, daily/monthly pricing, review details, neighbourhood info, room type/amenities, property IDs; supports regex filtering, date-range search, CSV/XLSX export, optional Elasticsearch indexing, GraphQL v3 API integration. No committed sample data.
candidates.why_useful: Second-highest-star pure scraper found; explicit note that Airbnb broke Scrapy-based requests is itself useful signal about how brittle these clients are (all of them are catalogue-only per the run's rules regardless).

candidates.name: actor-airbnb-scraper (dtrungtin)
candidates.what_it_holds: 30-star, 24-fork JavaScript Apify Actor (92 commits) with two modes: destination search (listing URL, name, star rating, guest capacity, address, review summary) and per-listing detail (full reviews with author/timestamp/rating, multi-currency pricing, host info, availability calendar). Runs on the Apify platform (paid credits, ~$1 per 1,000 results); source is open on GitHub.
candidates.why_useful: One of the most field-complete Airbnb search+detail scrapers found, and unlike most of the others it explicitly returns an availability calendar alongside multi-currency price — relevant to any future realised-ADR/occupancy reconstruction (gap #2) if a human authorizes running a hosted scraper.

candidates.name: airbnb-scraper (petrpatek)
candidates.what_it_holds: 11-star Apify public actor (JavaScript, updated Dec 2022) for scraping Airbnb home listings; overlaps closely with dtrungtin's actor above (both Apify-hosted, both destination+detail modes).
candidates.why_useful: Second independent Apify-based Airbnb actor; low marginal value once dtrungtin/actor-airbnb-scraper and omkarcloud/airbnb-scraper are catalogued, but confirms the field set (price, availability, reviews, host) is consistent across independent implementations.

candidates.name: airbnb-scraper (omkarcloud)
candidates.what_it_holds: Recently active repo (updated ~22 days before scout date; 5 stars, 4 commits) providing an API-style scraper covering 67 country domains. Fields: listing type/capacity/bedrooms/beds/baths, live nightly rate with breakdown (base, discounts, fees), real-time availability for given dates, host profile (superhost status, response rate, years hosting), amenities by category, review ratings incl. category sub-scores (cleanliness, accuracy, etc.), coordinates/address/place IDs, photos with captions, house rules/cancellation policy/sleeping arrangements. Extensive sample JSON responses in the README (documentation examples, not a committed dataset).
candidates.why_useful: Most field-rich single-listing schema found in this sweep (includes category-level review sub-scores and full cancellation-policy text, relevant to the RNPL/cancellation-distribution gap #3 if reconstructable from cancellation-policy metadata) and is one of the most recently updated repos surveyed.

candidates.name: airbnb-scraper (everythingscraper) — STR analytics
candidates.what_it_holds: Very small repo (0 stars, 2 commits) wrapping an Apify Actor that explicitly computes occupancy rate, ADR and RevPAR per listing from Airbnb's forward-looking 12-month calendar, plus day-by-day booking status/pricing for the full 12 months, listing amenities/images/coordinates/review counts, and optional full review text/host portfolio. README shows a worked sample row (Paris listing: 78% occupancy, EUR142.50 ADR, EUR111.15 RevPAR). No committed dataset; output goes to JSON via Apify (paid).
candidates.why_useful: Directly targets gap #2 (realised ADR/occupancy for STRs) by name and design — this is the first repo in the sweep whose stated purpose is computing ADR/occupancy/RevPAR from Airbnb calendar data rather than just listing fields, even though (a) it uses FORWARD calendar/asking-price data, not realised bookings, so it inherits the same asking-vs-realised-price gap the project already knows about, and (b) it is unrun/uncatalogued elsewhere and has essentially no traction (0 stars).
candidates.last_activity: recent (2 commits, undated but appears current)
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: conceptually same forward-calendar-price limitation as project's existing Inside Airbnb calendar work

candidates.name: how-to-scrape-airbnb (Oxylabs)
candidates.what_it_holds: Vendor (Oxylabs) tutorial repo (21 commits) using their paid Web Scraper API plus Python asyncio/aiohttp to pull Airbnb listing titles, nightly/total pricing, host URL, rating, review text/dates, and photos from both listing pages and paginated search results (up to 250 listings/search). No committed dataset.
candidates.why_useful: Another independent field-schema reference, but requires a paid third-party proxy/API service (Oxylabs), which is a heavier dependency than pyairbnb/gobnb which hit Airbnb directly.

candidates.name: scrapfly-scrapers: airbnb-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: One folder inside the large multi-site scrapfly-scrapers monorepo (Python 3.10, scrapfly-sdk, 1,028 commits repo-wide). Extracts search results by location, full listing detail (title, description, room type, amenities, images), host info + geo-coordinates, pricing/ratings/review counts, and guest review text. Includes a `./results` directory with committed example output (format unconfirmed — likely JSON) plus `airbnb.py`, `run.py`, `test.py`.
candidates.why_useful: Only repo in this sweep with an actual committed example-output folder (not just README samples) alongside the scraper code, and it is part of a monorepo that ALSO contains scrapers for Booking.com and other non-Airbnb travel sites (see companion candidate below) — useful as a template if the team later builds its own point-in-time Airbnb capture and wants a maintained anti-bot approach (relies on paid Scrapfly proxy/rendering, though).
candidates.time_coverage: live/point-of-scrape only; committed results are illustrative examples, not a time series
candidates.license: check repo (LICENSE file present, terms not confirmed)

candidates.name: scrapfly-scrapers (monorepo, booking-scraper + others)
candidates.what_it_holds: Multi-site scraper monorepo (Python, 1,028+ commits, LICENSE present) with per-site folders each containing `<site>.py`, `run.py`, `test.py`, and a `./results` example-output folder; confirmed folders include `airbnb-scraper` and `booking-scraper` (Booking.com hotel/apartment search+detail). Other travel-adjacent site folders likely present but not individually verified in this pass.
candidates.why_useful: A single maintained repo covering both Airbnb and at least one direct competitor (Booking.com) with a consistent scraper pattern and example outputs; worth a deeper look by whichever agent owns the competitor-OTA theme, since it lowers the engineering cost of building a comparable non-Airbnb capture (gap #9) using the same toolkit already catalogued for Airbnb.

candidates.name: airbnb-scraper (toniprada) — user profiles
candidates.what_it_holds: Small, old repo (8 stars, updated Jan 2017) that downloads Airbnb user/host profile pages rather than listings.
candidates.why_useful: Niche and stale (2017); host-profile scraping could theoretically feed a host-growth/supply proxy but the tool itself is unmaintained and pre-dates Airbnb's current API/anti-bot posture. Catalogued for completeness only.

candidates.name: airbnb-scraper (kailu3)
candidates.what_it_holds: 26-star Scrapy + ScrapySplash spider (Python, last updated Nov 2019).
candidates.why_useful: Old (2019) and likely broken against current Airbnb anti-bot measures given its age relative to the newer scrapers above; low incremental value beyond confirming the same basic field set (listing/search) existed in this form years ago.

candidates.name: airbnb-web-scaper (romanrosh)
candidates.what_it_holds: 12-star repo (Python, updated Jan 2019) described as 'Scraper and hotel API for data comparison' — appears to pair Airbnb scraping with a separate hotel-price API for cross-comparison.
candidates.why_useful: Potentially relevant to a nights/ADR cross-check between Airbnb and hotel pricing (peer readthrough context) but old (2019) and not independently verified beyond the search snippet.

candidates.name: airbnb-review-scraper (stayapi)
candidates.what_it_holds: 0-star repo (from GitHub topics listing) advertised as scraping Airbnb listing reviews in Python or Node.js 'no proxies, no CAPTCHAs.' Not independently verified beyond the topic-page description.
candidates.why_useful: If genuinely proxy-free, could be a lighter-weight review-text puller than the project's existing 123-market reviews pipeline — but unverified traction (0 stars) and not fetched directly in this pass; flagged for someone else to verify before relying on it.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: overlaps existing 123-market reviews-index pipeline in method, not verified as better

candidates.name: vrbo-api examples (StayingAPI)
candidates.what_it_holds: Documentation/examples repo (MIT, 3 commits) for StayingAPI's paid unified REST API, which normalizes Vrbo property data (name, nightly rate, availability calendar, amenities, photos, host info, reviews, multi-date/occupancy price quotes) into the SAME schema used for its Airbnb, Booking.com and Google Hotels endpoints. No data or credentials committed — code samples and endpoint references only; the actual SDK is a separate paid package (`@stayingapi/sdk`).
candidates.why_useful: Points to a commercial (not free) cross-platform normalization layer covering Vrbo — Airbnb's closest direct competitor supply-side (gap #9) — but it is a paid API, not open data, so value here is only as a pointer to what fields are obtainable, not a usable free source.
candidates.license: MIT (for the example code only; underlying API is paid)

candidates.name: Booking-dataset-sample (Bright Data / luminati-io)
candidates.what_it_holds: Committed CSV file 'Booking-dataset-sample Listings.csv' with 1,001 rows sampled from Bright Data's commercial Booking.com listings dataset (advertised at 30.4K+ records total, also offered in JSON/NDJSON/Parquet from the vendor, though only the CSV sample is actually in the repo). 25+ columns: title, address, city, image links, check-in/out params, adults/children/rooms, final_price, original_price, currency, tax description, bedroom/kitchen/living-room/bed counts, review_score, review_count, free_cancellation, no_prepayment flags. Geography/date not specified in the sample. Mirrored under near-identical repos bright-data-de/, bright-kr/, bright-jp/Booking-dataset-sample (localized-language versions of the same sample).
candidates.why_useful: A REAL committed dataset (not just a scraper) of Booking.com listings with price and cancellation-policy fields — directly touches gap #9 (competitor OTA supply) and gap #3 (cancellation-rate distributions, via the free_cancellation/no_prepayment flags), though only 1,001 rows as a promotional teaser for a paid larger dataset, no explicit date/geography stamp, and it's a single snapshot, not a time series.
candidates.license: Bright Data promotional sample; redistribution terms unclear, check before use

notes: IMPORTANT CAVEAT: this session's WebSearch tool budget was already exhausted (200/200) before this scout could run any of it -- every WebSearch call in this run returned a budget-exhausted error and zero results. All findings above came instead from WebFetch on github.com/search results pages and github.com/topics/* pages (both of which still worked and returned real repo listings), plus direct WebFetch verification of individual repo READMEs. This is a narrower discovery surface than a full web search sweep (misses Kaggle/Zenodo/HuggingFace/blog-post mentions entirely) so this theme should be re-run with real WebSearch once the session budget resets, especially to find: (a) any repo mirroring OLD Airbnb API responses as a static/historical dataset rather than a live client, (b) blog posts linking to less-discoverable scraper repos, (c) Kaggle/HuggingFace datasets built by running one of these scrapers historically. github.com/search also 429-rate-limited after ~3 rapid calls; topics pages did not, and were the more reliable channel. No committed, genuine historical Airbnb dataset was found in this theme -- every str_airbnb_direct repo here is a LIVE client/scraper (data_kind='acquisition_method'), consistent with the project's existing conclusion that current Airbnb calendars carry no realised price and any 'realised ADR' from these tools would only ever be forward asking-price data, same limitation as the team's existing Inside Airbnb work. Two genuinely different findings: (1) everythingscraper/airbnb-scraper is the first tool seen in any sweep whose explicit purpose is computing ADR/occupancy/RevPAR from Airbnb calendar data (still forward-looking, still Apify-paid, still 0-star/unproven) -- worth a note in the ADR workstream docs even if never run. (2) the Bright Data Booking-dataset-sample repos are actual committed CSVs (not just scrapers) with cancellation-policy flags, touching two gaps at once (#9 competitor OTA, #3 cancellation distributions) with only 1,001 undated rows -- flag to whoever owns the competitor-OTA or RNPL theme to check if Bright Data offers a larger/dated historical sample.
